entries.speaker: Moderator
entries.title: Moderator: ""Thank you, President Rayne.""
entries.dialogueText: "Thank you, President Rayne."

entries.speaker: Remus Holstron
entries.title: Remus Holstron: ""The others are afraid to say it, b..."
entries.dialogueText: "The others are afraid to say it, but Sordland's economy would soar to new heights if honest Sordish businesses weren't constantly being undercut by certain shady interlopers. You know who I mean."

entries.speaker: Moderator
entries.title: Moderator: ""Let's move on to the economy, then.""
entries.dialogueText: "Let's move on to the economy, then."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""That isn't exactly a priority for..."
entries.dialogueText: "That isn't exactly a priority for my party at the moment."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""The depression was the exclusive f..."
entries.dialogueText: "The depression was the exclusive fault of my former economic advisor Symon Holl. Things will run a lot more smoothly now that he's gone."
entries.menuText: "The depression was the exclusive fault of my former economic advisor Symon Holl. Things will run a lot more smoothly now that he's gone."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I promise I will aid Sordish worke..."
entries.dialogueText: "I promise I will aid Sordish workers affected by the depression."
entries.menuText: "I promise I will aid Sordish workers affected by the depression."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Slowly but surely, I am lifting So..."
entries.dialogueText: "Slowly but surely, I am lifting Sordland to economic greatness."
entries.menuText: "Slowly but surely, I am lifting Sordland to economic greatness."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Why fix what's not broken? As long..."
entries.dialogueText: "Why fix what's not broken? As long as I remain president, Sordland will never see another recession."
entries.menuText: "Why fix what's not broken? As long as I remain president, Sordland will never see another recession."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""My recovery was just the beginning..."
entries.dialogueText: "My recovery was just the beginning. If I stay president, Sordland will become one of the world's wealthiest nations."
entries.menuText: "My recovery was just the beginning. If I stay president, Sordland will become one of the world's wealthiest nations."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""The threat of recession is over, b..."
entries.dialogueText: "The threat of recession is over, but I will not rest until every Sord can enjoy the fruits of our recovery."
entries.menuText: "The threat of recession is over, but I will not rest until every Sord can enjoy the fruits of our recovery."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I'm doing the best I can given how..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm doing the best I can given how badly my predecessors screwed up. We're not in a depression, are we?"
entries.menuText: "I'm doing the best I can given how badly my predecessors screwed up. We're not in a depression, are we?"

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: ""The depression is but a minor bump..."
entries.dialogueText: "The depression is but a minor bump on the road to greatness. As long as we keep the government's firm hand on the steering wheel of our economy, this country will prosper as never before."

entries.speaker: Manoly Suheil
entries.title: Manoly Suheil: ""I couldn't agree more that Sordlan..."
entries.dialogueText: "I couldn't agree more that Sordland needs to help its working families. Which is why I will maintain and even increase President Rayne's tax hikes for its wealthiest corporations."

entries.speaker: Frens Ricter
entries.title: Frens Ricter: ""I couldn't agree more that Sordlan..."
entries.dialogueText: "I couldn't agree more that Sordland needs to help its working families. Which is why I've developed a comprehensive program of tax initiatives for small businesses."

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: ""The current recovery is nothing co..."
entries.dialogueText: "The current recovery is nothing compared to what I'll be able to achieve with the government's firm hand on the steering wheel of our economy."

entries.speaker: Moderator
entries.title: Moderator: ""How do each of you plan to bring t..."
entries.dialogueText: "How do each of you plan to bring the Sordish economy out of its current state of stasis?"

entries.speaker: Moderator
entries.title: Moderator: ""Now that recession is no longer a..."
entries.dialogueText: "Now that recession is no longer a threat, how will all of you bring the Sordish economy forward?"

entries.speaker: Moderator
entries.title: Moderator: ""I'm sure many of our viewers would..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm sure many of our viewers would like to know how you candidates are planning on ending the Sordish Depression."

entries.speaker: Mansoun Leke
entries.title: Mansoun Leke: ""Sordland is as wealthy as it needs..."
entries.dialogueText: "Sordland is as wealthy as it needs to be. Our task is to redistribute that wealth so that all citizens can prosper."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""Sordland is as wealthy as it needs..."
entries.dialogueText: "Sordland is as wealthy as it needs to be. Our task is to redistribute that wealth so that all citizens can prosper."

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: ""As long as we keep the government'..."
entries.dialogueText: "As long as we keep the government's firm hand on the steering wheel of our economy, this country will prosper as never before."

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: ""I tried to say this to President R..."
entries.dialogueText: "I tried to say this to President Rayne many times. With the government's firm hand on the steering wheel of our economy, this country will prosper as never before."

entries.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
entries.title: Kesaro Kibener: ""There is a massive potential in ou..."
entries.dialogueText: "There is a massive potential in our countries economic capacity. I would push for Autarky and transferring technological knowledge to our local industries. Sordland must control all strategic resources of production and be as independent as possible from foreign influences."

entries.speaker: Mansoun Leke
entries.title: Mansoun Leke: ""The first step is suspension of re..."
entries.dialogueText: "The first step is suspension of rent and mortgage payments and a ban on evictions. Then we would move on to job creation through public works programs."

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: ""As one of the individuals responsi..."
entries.dialogueText: "As one of the individuals responsible for Sordland's economic recovery, I feel uniquely qualified to answer this."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""The first step is suspension of re..."
entries.dialogueText: "The first step is suspension of rent and mortgage payments and a ban on evictions. Then we would move on to strengthening Sordland's labor unions."

entries.speaker: Mansoun Leke
entries.title: Mansoun Leke: ""Booming markets and increasing CEO..."
entries.dialogueText: "Booming markets and increasing CEO salaries aren't an indicator of whether regular Sordish workers can put food on their tables."

entries.speaker: Mansoun Leke
entries.title: Mansoun Leke: ""With all due respect, that isn't a..."
entries.dialogueText: "With all due respect, that isn't a priority for my party at the moment."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""The fact is, Rayne may have meant..."
entries.dialogueText: "The fact is, Rayne may have meant well, but he left millions of working-class Sords in need of urgent, immediate aid."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "He looked at the camera."
entries.dialogueText: He looked at the camera.

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""The fact is, Rayne's incompetence..."
entries.dialogueText: "The fact is, Rayne's incompetence left millions of working-class Sords in need of urgent, immediate aid."

entries.speaker: Mansoun Leke
entries.title: Mansoun Leke: ""Thank you for asking. President Ra..."
entries.dialogueText: "Thank you for asking. President Rayne's mishandling of our economy has left millions of working-class Sords, especially minorities, in need of urgent, immediate aid."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Lileas sniffed."
entries.dialogueText: Lileas sniffed.

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""Booming markets and increasing CEO..."
entries.dialogueText: "Booming markets and increasing CEO salaries aren't an indicator of whether regular Sordish workers can put food on their tables."

entries.speaker: Frens Ricter
entries.title: Frens Ricter: ""I will also implement a market eco..."
entries.dialogueText: "I will also implement a market economy in Sordland, with state intervention as necessary to ensure the free market produces results close to its theoretical potential."

entries.speaker: Frens Ricter
entries.title: Frens Ricter: ""I believe President Rayne pointed..."
entries.dialogueText: "I believe President Rayne pointed us in the right direction with a market economy, but state intervention is needed to ensure the free market produces results close to its theoretical potential."

entries.speaker: Manoly Suheil
entries.title: Manoly Suheil: ""I will also initiate a series of m..."
entries.dialogueText: "I will also initiate a series of massive redevelopment projects to promote growth and stability to rural regions."

entries.speaker: Frens Ricter
entries.title: Frens Ricter: ""Of course, I would immediately und..."
entries.dialogueText: "Of course, I would immediately undo the president's nationalization of our major corporations."

entries.speaker: Frens Ricter
entries.title: Frens Ricter: ""And I would continue and expand up..."
entries.dialogueText: "And I would continue and expand upon the privatization of our major corporations."

entries.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
entries.title: Kesaro Kibener: ""We must increase our economic capa..."
entries.dialogueText: "We must increase our economic capabilities to then turn our goods into quality yet affordable export materials for other developing nations. I would also impose high taxes on the rich to fund military industrial research and development."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "He looked pointedly at Mansoun. The..."
entries.dialogueText: He looked pointedly at Mansoun. The WPB leader gritted his teeth but refused to take the bait.

entries.speaker: Remus Holstron
entries.title: Remus Holstron: ""My economic plan is focused on kee..."
entries.dialogueText: "My economic plan is focused on keeping Sordish money inside Sordish borders. Raising import tariffs would be a start, as would higher taxes on businesses owned by foreigners."

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: ""That means undoing the disastrous..."
entries.dialogueText: "That means undoing the disastrous free market reforms of Rayne and Alphonso."

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: ""As well as seizing the assets of S..."
entries.dialogueText: "As well as seizing the assets of Sordland's wealthiest corporations so that oligarchs can no longer hold more power than the state."

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: ""That means continuing with a plann..."
entries.dialogueText: "That means continuing with a planned economy, as Soll had intended."

entries.speaker: Lileas Graf
entries.title: Lileas Graf: ""As well as seizing the assets of S..."
entries.dialogueText: "As well as seizing the assets of Sordland's wealthiest corporations so that oligarchs can no longer hold more power than the state."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""The real danger to our economy is..."
entries.dialogueText: "The real danger to our economy is the Sordish oligarchs. No one man must be allowed to hold so much wealth."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Denis made a scoffing sound."
entries.dialogueText: Denis made a scoffing sound.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""The Oligarchs are no threat anymor..."
entries.dialogueText: "The Oligarchs are no threat anymore. I saw to that."
entries.menuText: "The Oligarchs are no threat anymore. I saw to that."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""The Oligarchs do more for Sordland..."
entries.dialogueText: "The Oligarchs do more for Sordland than you ever will."
entries.menuText: "The Oligarchs do more for Sordland than you ever will."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""The Oligarchs are the engine that..."
entries.dialogueText: "The Oligarchs are the engine that keeps our economy running."
entries.menuText: "The Oligarchs are the engine that keeps our economy running."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""They're gone, remember? Prison, et..."
entries.dialogueText: "They're gone, remember? Prison, et cetera...?"
entries.menuText: "They're gone, remember? Prison, et cetera...?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Marcel Koronti has done more for S..."
entries.dialogueText: "Marcel Koronti has done more for Sordland than you ever will."
entries.menuText: "Marcel Koronti has done more for Sordland than you ever will."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Marcel isn't so bad...""
entries.dialogueText: "Marcel isn't so bad..."
entries.menuText: "Marcel isn't so bad..."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Walter Tusk has done more for Sord..."
entries.dialogueText: "Walter Tusk has done more for Sordland than you ever will."
entries.menuText: "Walter Tusk has done more for Sordland than you ever will."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Walter isn't so bad...""
entries.dialogueText: "Walter isn't so bad..."
entries.menuText: "Walter isn't so bad..."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I agree. They must be stopped.""
entries.dialogueText: "I agree. They must be stopped."
entries.menuText: "I agree. They must be stopped."

entries.speaker: Player_Italic
entries.title: Player_Italic: "I refrained from commenting."
entries.dialogueText: I refrained from commenting.
entries.menuText: Say nothing.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The moderator cleared her throat."
entries.dialogueText: The moderator cleared her throat.

entries.speaker: Moderator
entries.title: Moderator: ""Yes, let's leave Marcel Koronti ou..."
entries.dialogueText: "Yes, let's leave Marcel Koronti out of this, shall we?"

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The moderator cleared her throat."
entries.dialogueText: The moderator cleared her throat.

entries.speaker: Moderator
entries.title: Moderator: ""We're getting off-track.""
entries.dialogueText: "We're getting off-track."

entries.speaker: Moderator
entries.title: Moderator: ""Mr. President, would you care to c..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. President, would you care to comment on your plans for the economy?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""As I said earlier, my plan for a g..."
entries.dialogueText: "As I said earlier, my plan for a guaranteed living wage for everyone will lead to unprecedented prosperity."
entries.menuText: "As I said earlier, my plan for a guaranteed living wage for everyone will lead to unprecedented prosperity."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""As I said earlier, my plan for a n..."
entries.dialogueText: "As I said earlier, my plan for a nuclear program will lead to unprecedented prosperity."
entries.menuText: "As I said earlier, my plan for a nuclear program will lead to unprecedented prosperity."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""As I said earlier, my plan for a s..."
entries.dialogueText: "As I said earlier, my plan for a space program will lead to unprecedented prosperity."
entries.menuText: "As I said earlier, my plan for a space program will lead to unprecedented prosperity."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Just trust me. If we keep sticking..."
entries.dialogueText: "Just trust me. If we keep sticking to my plan, the economy will bounce back."
entries.menuText: "Just trust me. If we keep sticking to my plan, the economy will bounce back."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""My opponents' plans would only thr..."
entries.dialogueText: "My opponents' plans would only thrust us deeper into recession. We must stay on the course I have plotted."
entries.menuText: "My opponents' plans would only thrust us deeper into recession. We must stay on the course I have plotted."

entries.speaker: Frens Ricter
entries.title: Frens Ricter: ""And I would continue Alphonso's pr..."
entries.dialogueText: "And I would continue Alphonso's privatization of our major corporations. The sole thing his administration got right."

entries.speaker: Manoly Suheil
entries.title: Manoly Suheil: ""I couldn't agree more that Sordlan..."
entries.dialogueText: "I couldn't agree more that Sordland needs to help its working families. We can pay for their aid by raising taxes on the country's largest corporations."

entries.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
entries.title: Kesaro Kibener: ""On top of that I would remove Rayn..."
entries.dialogueText: "On top of that I would remove Rayne's ridiculous 'vice' tax so that Sords can once more enjoy an affordable drink and a smoke after a long working day."

entries.speaker: Remus Holstron
entries.title: Remus Holstron: ""With that money flowing, I'll be a..."
entries.dialogueText: "With that money flowing, I'll be able to remove Rayne's ridiculous 'vice' tax so that Sords can once more enjoy an affordable drink and a smoke after a long working day. As is their God-given right."

entries.speaker: Mansoun Leke
entries.title: Mansoun Leke: ""Free public transit and prescripti..."
entries.dialogueText: "Free public transit and prescription drugs -- that's a very good start. But there's much more we could do."

entries.speaker: Mansoun Leke
entries.title: Mansoun Leke: ""Free prescription drugs for all --..."
entries.dialogueText: "Free prescription drugs for all -- that's a very good start. But there's much more we could do."

entries.dialogueText: "Taxing luxury goods -- that's a start. But there's much more we could do."

entries.dialogueText: "Free public transit for all -- that's a start. But there's much more we could do."

entries.dialogueText: "Taxing luxury goods -- that's a start. But there's much more we could do."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""The real danger to our economy are..."
entries.dialogueText: "The real danger to our economy are the oligarchs like the Koronti family. These jackals disrupt, break and change the system in their favour and disregard the people."
